items.stem: On a construction site, the hierarchy of controls is applied to a recurring fall hazard at an unprotected leading edge. Which control should a supervisor pursue first?

options.text: Eliminate the hazard by redesigning the task so work at the edge is not required
options.rationale: Correct: elimination sits at the top of the hierarchy of controls and removes the hazard rather than relying on the worker.

options.text: Issue personal fall-arrest harnesses to the crew
options.rationale: PPE is the lowest level of the hierarchy and is used only when higher-order controls are not feasible.

options.text: Post a warning sign at the leading edge
options.rationale: Administrative controls rank below elimination, substitution and engineering controls.

options.text: Hold a toolbox talk about fall awareness
options.rationale: Training is an administrative control and does not remove the hazard.

items.explanation: Correct: elimination sits at the top of the hierarchy of controls and removes the hazard rather than relying on the worker.

items.stem: A supervisor is determining who is responsible for inspecting a scaffold before each work shift. Which approach is consistent with a competent-person requirement?

options.text: A person able to identify hazards and authorized to take prompt corrective action inspects it
options.rationale: Correct: a competent person is defined by both the ability to recognize hazards and the authority to correct them.

options.text: Any available worker performs the inspection to save time
options.rationale: Inspection by an untrained worker does not satisfy the competent-person standard.

options.text: Inspection is only required weekly once the scaffold is built
options.rationale: Scaffolds require inspection before each shift and after events that could affect integrity, not merely weekly.

options.text: The equipment rental company is solely responsible on site
options.rationale: Responsibility on the active work site rests with the employer's competent person, not the supplier.

items.explanation: Correct: a competent person is defined by both the ability to recognize hazards and the authority to correct them.

items.stem: Select TWO conditions that, by themselves, generally require protective systems before workers enter an excavation.

options.text: The excavation is 5 feet (1.5 m) or more deep in soil that is not stable rock
options.rationale: Correct: depth at or above this threshold in non-stable-rock soil generally triggers a protective system requirement.

options.text: A competent person identifies signs of a potential cave-in at any depth
options.rationale: Correct: observed cave-in indicators require protection regardless of the depth threshold.

options.text: The excavation will be open for less than one hour
options.rationale: Short duration alone does not remove the need for a protective system.

options.text: Only experienced workers will enter the excavation
options.rationale: Worker experience does not substitute for sloping, shoring or shielding.

options.text: The spoil pile is placed at the edge of the excavation
options.rationale: Placing spoil at the edge increases risk; it is a hazard, not a condition that makes protection optional.

items.explanation: Correct: depth at or above this threshold in non-stable-rock soil generally triggers a protective system requirement.
